newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar gains as demand rises ahead of strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar gains as demand rises ahead of strike.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Thursday rose as a planned transport strike next week saw consumer demand rise and more offtake by bulk consumers, dealers said. Arrivals remained low.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 10 rupees at 1,280/1,310 rupees per quintal while M-30 climbed up by the same margin at 1,315/1,400 rupees per quintal.
"The demand for sugar turned higher ahead of the indefinite strike called by the Indian transport operators," one broker said.
"Every buyer now wants to buy as much as possible before the strike commences as they were fear shortages in the coming days due to the proposed strike," he added.
Indian transport operators have planned an indefinite strike from April to protest against the imposition of a service tax and a hike in the insurance premium.
Overall market sentiments remained firm at the close of the session on reports that some of transport operators have hiked freight charges from mills to the market ahead of next week's agitation.
